title: Chapter 6 — Convocation
description: Final year. Fees, results, Dubai's last offer, Tamara's question, and a woman at the gate with a cooler of pap.

cards.title: Final year
cards.text: Four years. One more semester. One more chance to become whoever you've been pretending to be — or to stop.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Suspended for a semester, you came back quieter. People still whisper. You let them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The panel never found anything. You still check the door every time someone knocks.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Owó Ńlá's ₦100,000 arrives every month, on time, like guilt.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Expelled. The letter was one paragraph long. You read it forty times anyway.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You still hang around the back gate. Spike thinks that's funny. Dubai thinks it's an opportunity.

beats.speaker: babaGate
beats.text: (at the bursary window, reading a list) Somtochukwu Eze. Outstanding fees: {schoolFees}. No clearance, no gown. No gown, no convocation. Next!

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: (The queue behind you is breathing on your neck.)

options.text: Pay it from your savings.
Call Hon. Ronke. She offered you an internship once — she meant it.
options.lockedText: Only if you told her mother the truth

options.text: Let Tamara pay. She's been offering for a year.
Sell the akara brand to the cafeteria. Every last recipe.
options.lockedText: You'd need a business to sell

options.text: Take one big job from Dubai. Just one.
Walk away from the window.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Final results are pasted on the notice board. Two hundred people push to read one sheet of paper.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Your CGPA: {stat:cgpa}.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You know exactly which grades you earned and which ones you bought. The sheet doesn't.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Not one handout bought. Not one leaked question. Every point on that sheet is yours.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: ECO 201 — you aced it fair and square. Dr. Fasanya's replacement wrote 'Excellent' in red.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That GST failure still sits there like a stain. You carried it through four years.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Your missing script from second year is still missing. Someone got your A.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Half the names on the list you tutored. Some of them wave at you.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The class strike you organized got the exam rescheduled — the whole class remembers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Professor's Expo pass from first year: still the luckiest grade you ever got.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: Somto! Or should I say 'Bonny Deep Energy'? (He laughs.) I never told anyone, you know. Four years.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: Somto. Final year. You know, you still haven't told me one true thing about your family.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: Remember first week? You said 'I'm from Iyana-Wahala, my mum sells pap.' I thought you were joking. You were the only one not joking.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: Akara King! The cafeteria still uses your recipe. Badly.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: And you never let them call you 'Oil Money'. I respect that.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: They still talk about the night the Dons cornered you by the chapel.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: They still talk about the night you outran the Dons by the chapel.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: And you missed my birthday in second year. I've forgiven you. I've mentioned it 300 times, but I've forgiven you.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: The in-crowd's throwing a final-year party at the Lekki house. You're invited — of course.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: You were always half in, half out with those rich kids. Final year: pick a side.

beats.speaker: tobi
beats.text: Since the first week, when everyone found out you were from the bus stop, you stopped pretending. Best thing that ever happened to you.

beats.speaker: dubai
beats.text: Somto. Last time I'll ask. One transfer. Five million. Then you never see me again.

variants.text: You laughed at me in first year. Look at me now. Look at you. One transfer, five million. Laugh now.
Partner. The Agency is sniffing round the hostel. One last big one, then we disappear.

beats.speaker: dubai
beats.text: And don't forget: I know about the bus stop. One phone call to your fancy girlfriend's mother.

beats.speaker: dubai
beats.text: Your loan app's still chasing you, abi? Pay them with this.

beats.speaker: dubai
beats.text: You've done small ones with me before. This is just bigger.

beats.speaker: dubai
beats.text: (He's holding out a phone with an account number already typed in.)

options.text: Take the job.
"No. Never."

cards.title: 3:12 a.m.
cards.text: Boots in the corridor. Torchlight under the door. 'TASK FORCE! EVERYBODY OUT!'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You stop running behind the chapel. Your lungs are on fire. Dubai's phone is in your pocket. Dubai is not.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A cell with thirty men and one window. Somebody's radio is playing the convocation livestream. You hear your classmates' names called, one by one.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mama visits on Thursday. She sold the freezer to pay for your first year. She brings pap in a flask.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mama visits on Thursday. She brings pap in a flask. She doesn't say anything. She doesn't have to.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: (at the car park) So. Convocation.

variants.text: (at the car park) You warned me about Owó Ńlá when it cost you everything. I haven't forgotten. Convocation, then.
(at the car park, not looking at you) My mother says your 'scholarship' sponsor knew things only I knew. Funny that.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: I liked you from the first day. Even though you lied about the oil thing.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: You told me the truth on the first day and I didn't believe you. That's on me.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: The first day, you warned me about the Dons. Nobody else did.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: My mother still talks about that dinner. 'The oil boy.' She liked you. She liked the you that doesn't exist.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: My mother never trusted you after that dinner.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: You kept lying. Even when I gave you every chance.

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: (She's holding two invitations: one to her family's table at convocation, one blank.)

options.text: "Sit with my mother at convocation. Meet the real me."
options.lockedText: She'd have to know the truth first

options.text: "Your family's table. Of course."
"I think we should stop."

beats.speaker: ife
beats.text: Dr. Fasanya's gone. Did you hear? Suspended, then sacked. Seven girls have come forward since.

beats.speaker: ife
beats.text: You still have that recording, don't you? He's still teaching. He's still 'sorting'.

beats.speaker: ife
beats.text: I recorded him myself in the end. Somebody had to.

beats.speaker: ife
beats.text: You helped me when no one else would. I won't forget it.

beats.speaker: ife
beats.text: You told me to just pay him. I didn't. I'm graduating with a 2:2 and my dignity.

beats.speaker: ife
beats.text: You told me to stay out of it. I couldn't.

beats.speaker: ife
beats.text: "The campus paper wants to run the full story. With your name next to mine. Will you?"

options.text: "Put my name on it."
"Leave me out of it."

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: Capo. (He's bowing. To you.) The boys await your instructions.

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: You beat me in front of the boys. Nobody's done that. I don't like you. But I respect you.

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: Still limping from our little talk? Good.

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: You named me to the VC. I was suspended for a year. I'm back.

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: You reported us in first year. The VC lost the file. Funny how files go missing.

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: You turned us down twice. Once at the initiation, once for that job. Brave or stupid.

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: You walked away from the back gate. Everybody walks back eventually.

beats.speaker: spike
beats.text: Brother. Once a Don, always a Don.

cards.title: Convocation day
cards.text: Gowns. Drums. Aunties in matching aso-ebi. Somewhere near the gate, a woman in her best wrapper is holding a cooler of pap like a trophy.

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: (at the gate, carrying a cooler) Somto! I came early! I brought pap for your friends!

variants.text: (at the gate, smaller somehow) You told me not to come to your matriculation. I'm here now. I won't embarrass you. I'll stand at the back.
(at the gate) The last time I came, you told your friends I was your 'house help'. I came anyway. A mother comes anyway.
(at the gate, waving with both hands) My son! The graduate! Where are your friends? Bring them! I brought pap!

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: I sold the freezer. I'd sell it again.

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: Quickcash people called my phone. They called me a debtor's mother. Somto, what did you do?

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: And you paid back that loan. I'm proud of that too.

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: You promised me you'd make me proud. You promised in front of the whole bus stop.

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: You told me to wait at the gate on the first day. I'm still at the gate.

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: You said you'd hide where you came from. Did you manage it?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You're still carrying the designer bag. It's starting to peel.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You're still carrying the nylon bag from home. You never got another one.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: (Your classmates are walking past. Tamara's family is coming this way.)

options.text: Hug her. Introduce her to everyone. "This is my mother. She sells pap."
Take her to a quiet corner, away from everyone.
Pretend you don't know her.

beats.speaker: ronke
beats.text: (arriving with Tamara) Somto! And... who is this?

beats.speaker: tamara
beats.text: (to Mama, holding out both hands) Ma, I've heard so much about your pap.

beats.speaker: ronke
beats.text: (not unkindly) Oh. So THIS is Bonny Deep Energy. (A long pause, then she laughs.) My father sold palm oil at Oyingbo. Welcome, Madam.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The VC is calling names. Yours is next — or it would be, if there was a name to call.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The VC is calling names. Yours is next.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: (Everything you've done leads here.)

options.text: Collect the First Class certificate. Earned.
Walk the stage. Wave at Mama in the crowd.
options.lockedText: Needs your degree and Mama beside you

options.text: Walk the stage. Then the Lekki party. The lie is your life now.
Skip the stage. Stand with Ife and the press outside the senate.
Take the Capo's seat at the back gate.
options.lockedText: Needs to be the Capo's right hand

options.text: Get into Owó Ńlá's car. A job in politics is waiting.
options.lockedText: Owó Ńlá doesn't know your name

options.text: Get on the night bus to Cotonou with Dubai's money.
Leave the campus for good.
Take the danfo back to Iyana-Wahala.
